recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not change current FHIR source for FHIR-20465; any future desire to correct historical R4/R4B/R5 package surfaces should be handled as a separate publication/tooling task.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-I correction for FHIR 4.0.0 definitions JSON where Element.id's base/differential metadata disagreed with snapshots for Element subtypes; the resolution said the differential was correct and snapshots needed correction, Applied for R5.
initial_application: No FHIR core source commit directly tagged FHIR-20465 was found. The relevant source history after the issue is the 2019-12-10 abstract type framework rebuild; current active datatype source defines Element.@id as type string and lets BackboneElement inherit it without a separate id row.
additional_context: The original Zulip thread supports the same conclusion that official generated snapshots were malformed if they replaced inherited Element.id metadata. Later same-family id metadata issues are already represented on the combined branch. Historical R4/R4B/R5 release artifacts vary in fhir-type details, but Jira explicitly notes no likely R4/R4B technical correction and current source reconciliation should not edit old published release caches.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current build-scope source and current build.fhir.org profile/definitions outputs show Element.id, BackboneElement.id, PrimitiveType.id, string.id, and boolean.id as System.String with structuredefinition-fhir-type string, satisfying the current-build form of the issue.
